issues.failure_explanation: The displayed inequality claims the indefinite boundary form b_{\Gamma} is bounded below by positive terms. But b_{\Gamma} is linear in the trial stress and normal velocity; taking \bu_f^{\mathrm{S}}=0 and p^{\mathrm{S}}=0 gives b_{\Gamma}=0, while the right-hand side can be positive for any nonzero normal test combination. Thus the lower bound is false, and the coercivity conclusion for A is not established by this proof.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the false lower bound by the correct trace/Young estimate with negative terms and absorb those terms using a_f^S and the Nitsche penalty under the stated gamma condition.
issues.overall_effect: The coercivity of the spatial operator A is unsupported, affecting the DAE invertibility, semi-discrete and fully discrete well-posedness, stability, and error estimates that invoke it.
issues.title: Coercivity proof uses false lower bound for interface term
issues.why_classification: The defect is a central proof step, but the intended coercivity can likely be recovered by a contained correction of the boundary estimate and absorption; no global architecture change is obviously required.

issues.failure_explanation: Lemma usual_inf gives an inf-sup estimate with the supremum over all \mathbf{V}_h. The proof of inf_sup restricts the test space to the proper subspace \mathbf{V}_{h,0} and still asserts the same lower bound. Since a supremum over a subset can only be smaller, this inference is invalid; an inf-sup condition on \mathbf{V}_{h,0} is not proved.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Provide a genuine inf-sup proof for the restricted space \mathbf{V}_{h,0} or modify the argument so that the standard inf-sup is applied only on the full space.
issues.overall_effect: The LBB condition for the Nitsche-coupled operator B is unsupported, so the DAE invertibility, well-posedness, stability, and error estimates that use it are unreliable.
issues.title: Inf-sup proof applies Lemma usual_inf on a restricted subspace
issues.why_classification: The missing inf-sup condition is central to the saddle-point well-posedness and to later stability and error analysis; repairing it requires a new nontrivial LBB argument.

issues.failure_explanation: For the claimed block form, the bottom-left block must be the negative transpose of \mathbf{B}^T. The displayed bottom rows of \mathbf{N} omit the transposed entries involving \mathcal{C}_{s,\Gamma} and \mathcal{B}_{s}^{\mathrm{P}} and have sign mismatches for \mathcal{C}_{f,\Gamma} and \mathcal{C}_{p,\Gamma}. Thus the matrix used in the proof does not satisfy the saddle-point structure required to invoke Lemma invertibilty1.

failure_location.quote:
We readily note that the  matrix $\mathbf{M}+\mathbf{N}$  
yields a generalized saddle-point structure 
of the form 
\[
\mathbf{M} + \mathbf{N}
=
\begin{pmatrix}
\mathbf{A} & \mathbf{B}^T\\
-\mathbf{B}    & \mathbf{C}
\end{pmatrix},
\]

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the matrix display so that the bottom-left block is exactly the negative transpose of \mathbf{B}^T, or reprove invertibility for the actual matrix without assuming the displayed saddle-point form.
issues.overall_effect: The DAE invertibility argument for \mathbf{M}+\mathbf{N} and the fully discrete uniqueness proof relying on it are not justified.
issues.title: Displayed DAE matrix does not have the claimed saddle-point structure
issues.why_classification: The defect is a concrete matrix mismatch in a central proof, but a local correction of the displayed block or a direct invertibility argument can avoid changing the overall method.

issues.failure_explanation: The term (w\cdot\nabla u,u) vanishes only under additional divergence-free and boundary conditions on w. The fixed velocity w lies in \mathbf{K}_h, a discrete velocity space with only a norm bound; it is not required to be divergence-free. Hence the term is not identically zero and cannot be dropped in the uniqueness energy balance.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Keep the Oseen term in the energy estimate and bound it using the smallness of w in \mathbf{K}_h, then absorb it into the coercive terms.
issues.overall_effect: The uniqueness part of Theorem E+H is not established as written.
issues.title: Uniqueness proof sets a nonvanishing Oseen term to zero
issues.why_classification: The missing term can likely be controlled by the same smallness condition used for coercivity, but the current proof incorrectly discards it.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: for a given $\bw^{\mathrm{S}}_{f,h} \in \mathbf{K}_h$, the function $\bu^{\mathrm{S}}_{f,h}$ denotes the first component of the solution to the linearised version of problem~\eqref{semi_weak_for}

issues.failure_explanation: \mathbf{K}_h is a subset of the spatial finite element space \mathbf{V}_{f,h}, but the linearised problem is a time-dependent evolution problem. Its first component \bu_{f,h}^{\mathrm{S}} is a function of time, not an element of \mathbf{K}_h. Thus the map \mathcal{J}_h:\mathbf{K}_h\to\mathbf{K}_h is not well-defined. The contraction proof also assumes \mathcal{J}_h(\bw_2)\in\mathbf{K}_h without proving invariance.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define the fixed-point operator on an appropriate time-dependent function space (for example, a bounded subset of W^{1,\infty}(0,T;\mathbf{V}_{f,h})) and prove invariance and contraction in that space.
issues.overall_effect: The Banach fixed-point proof of well-posedness for the semi-discrete Nitsche scheme is invalid.
issues.title: Fixed-point operator is defined on a spatial set but maps to time-dependent solutions
issues.why_classification: The central fixed-point construction is type-mismatched; repairing it requires reworking the well-posedness proof in a time-dependent function space.

issues.failure_explanation: Scaling \mathbf{M} by 1/\tau changes the A block and hence the coercivity and kernel hypotheses; nonsingularity of \mathbf{M}+\mathbf{N} does not automatically transfer to (1/\tau)\mathbf{M}+\mathbf{N}. Moreover the nonlinear coefficient in the fully discrete scheme is \bu_{f,h}^{\mathrm{S},n-1}, while the stated smallness assumption is on \bu_{f,h}^{\mathrm{S},n}; the first step n=1 is therefore not covered.

failure_location.quote: Consider the matrix obtained from \eqref{discrete_matrix} by scaling the matrix $\mathbf{M}$ by $\frac{1}{\tau}$ and adding it to $\mathbf{N}$. This resulting matrix has the same structure as $\mathbf{M} + \mathbf{N}$, which is shown to be nonsingular in the proof of Lemma~\ref{invertibilty}. Therefore, the scaled matrix is nonsingular, and so is the matrix in \eqref{mixed-primal}.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Verify the positivity and kernel conditions for (1/\tau)\mathbf{M}+\mathbf{N} directly and state the smallness assumption on the coefficient \bu_{f,h}^{\mathrm{S},n-1} (including the initial value for n=1).
issues.overall_effect: Uniqueness of the fully discrete scheme is not established by the given proof.
issues.title: Fully discrete uniqueness proof does not establish nonsingularity of the actual matrix
issues.why_classification: The result may still be true, but the proof needs a direct nonsingularity argument for the scaled matrix and a corrected smallness hypothesis.

issues.failure_explanation: The projection \bPi_{r,h} is unweighted: it preserves (\nabla\cdot v,q), not (\nabla\cdot(\phi v),q). Hence b_f^{\mathrm{P}}(\chi_{r,h},\phi_{pp,h}) need not vanish when \phi varies. Similarly, Q_{p,h} is the unweighted L^2 projection, so the weighted inner product ((1-\phi)^2K^{-1}\chi_{pp,h},\phi_{pp,h}) is not zero in general. Hypothesis H1 permits nonconstant \phi.

failure_location.quote:
b^{\mathrm{S}}(\bchi_{f,h}^n, \phi_{f p, h}^n) =b_f^{\mathrm{P}}(\bchi_{r,h}^n, \phi_{p p, h}^n)= b_f^{\mathrm{P}}(\bphi_{r,h}^n, \chi_{pp,h}^n) =0, \\ 
((1-\phi)^2 K^{-1} d_{\tau} \chi_{p p,h}^n, \phi_{p p, h}^n) = 0.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either introduce weighted projection operators adapted to the coefficients \phi and (1-\phi)^2/K, or retain the extra weighted approximation terms and estimate them with the available approximation properties.
issues.overall_effect: Several simplifications in the error equation are false, so the proof of the a priori error estimate in Theorem appendix_fully is invalid.
issues.title: Error proof treats unweighted projection orthogonality as valid for weighted poroelastic forms
issues.why_classification: The false simplifications are local to the error proof and can likely be replaced by additional approximation estimates, but the current proof does not establish the stated error bound.
